lesson_title: The Post That Is Secretly a String
hook_text: The upright in the middle of a roof truss is not holding the roof up. It is hanging on for dear life.
clip_script: Every roof in the country is a triangle of timber called a truss, and every piece in it is either pulled or pushed. Pulled is tension, pushed is compression. The sloping rafters carry the roof, so they are pushed: compression. The flat beam along the bottom stops the rafters sliding apart and shoving the walls over, so it is pulled: tension. Now the upright in the middle, the king post. Everyone thinks it holds the roof up. Wrong. The roof is already carried by the rafters. The king post hangs from the top and holds the bottom beam up so it does not sag. It is pulled. It is tension. You could replace it with a string and the truss would still work. Try that with a rafter and the roof is on the floor. Pulled or pushed: once you can see it, you can read any structure.
visual_style: Whiteboard truss outline; rafters glow with inward arrows, tie beam with outward arrows; the king post becomes a dashed string and the truss holds; a rafter becomes string and the truss collapses.
pacing: Define the two words, label three members, the king post reveal, the string test.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and label every member of a king post truss with T or C.
